> 
> # **New Qwen Command Prompt System (V3)**
> 
> 
> Qwen's command prompts differ from those of V2 and V1, i.e., the Stable Diffusion system. While the textual content of the Stable Diffusion system is also adopted, it is not fully implemented. **For V2 Prompting, please use the [V2 Guide & Forum](https://discord.com/channels/1108377954389594236/1343317636888399884/1343317636888399884)**
> 
> *What works in V2 and V3 doesn't necessarily work in Qwen (V3) and vice versa.*
> 
> Qwen's command prompts differ from those of V2 and V1, i.e., the Stable Diffusion system. 
> 
> **What's different?**
> 
> - Qwen extracts its information from pure text.
> - Qwen can do a lot with full-text bullet points and lists.
> 
> Full-text example:
> `The hall is filled with people in the background, but the focus is on the subject.`
> 
> Bullet point or short information system:
> `wearing fitted white tank top, loose-fitting athletic pants, silver necklace, sunglasses.`
> 
> List system:
> `Background:
> - many people
> - large hall
> - dimly lit`
> 
> - No weighting/intensification of prompts is possible anymore except with words.
> - : Colons are for categories and only serve this purpose.
> 
> **What's NOT possible?**
> 
> - () Parentheses no longer have any use except for a slight separation function; there is NO change in importance (no weighting).
> - :1.2 ​​These weighting/intensification indicators have no effect in Qwen.
> 
> **Special Possibilities:**
> 
> With Qwen, you can add text to an image, for example, to a sign, a trailer, or anything else you can think of.
> 
> This text must be specially marked.
> `Sign by the roadside: "Stop, there are moose here"`
> 
> "" marks text... the colon (:) connects it to the sign.
> 
> It works with many things, and Qwen can sometimes even create something like this from messages.
> 
>

messages.author: ᒍᑌᖇᗩI
messages.content:
Here's a summary of what <@1380439356975878229>  and I have discovered:

The avatar/reference image dictates the maximum accuracy of the generator... and the generator attempts to compensate for blurriness and low sharpness with drawing styles.

This means: Lower quality and blurriness in the avatar image results in a significantly higher drawing style.

The sharper and more detailed the avatar image, the more realistic the output can be.

The inconsistency between the styles likely arises from the repeated analysis of the avatar image with each generation, which always perceives the "block"/"maximum detail" slightly differently. This is where the inconsistency comes from.

Background blurriness or partial blurriness also has an influence on the result and enhances the drawing style output.

This explains why an anime character cannot be rendered in great detail and why a blurry photo, even if somewhat indistinct, doesn't produce a realistic output.


These styles are not always accurate. The system probably acts like this:
reading the Avatar image... blurring creates the block... compensated for by drawing -> output image
reading Avatar image again... slightly different blurring result... new block... different compensation with drawing -> next output image

The best output with the Advanced Prompt Settings (as far as I've found) can be achieved with the following input:

`style:
- professional lifestyle photography
- professional lifestyle photography
- professional lifestyle photography`

Thanks to <@1380439356975878229>  for the help

This means that the Advanced Prompt Settings cannot override the style described in the image, nor the prompts themselves. They are blocked. Direct manual changes are possible.

If there are two descriptions in the image prompt, it always seems to refer to the most unrealistic one—the one that looks more like drawing.

This means this block is only responsible for Advanced Prompt Settings.

However, there isn't a limitation of Advanced Prompt Settings because other things like hair color and many others are quite easy to change using the prompt suffix in Advanced Prompt Settings.

Only the style is barely changeable, which is annoying.

So, the problem doesn't seem to be too many prompts in the image. It only directly affects the style. or rather that only one style can be active, and preferably the low-quality character style.

> 
> ## Avatar image and Qwen (V3)
> 
> 
> 
> Qwen has excellent image recognition, which is reflected very well in the output, but what do you need to be aware of?
> 
> - Unlike V2, image recognition isn't solely focused on the face; it also captures the body and uses a **style recognition**.
> 
> - I still recommend an image that meets certain criteria similar to V2, but Qwen is significantly more forgiving than V2.
> 
> 1. The face should be viewed as frontally as possible.
> 2. The larger and more accurately the face is recognized, the better Qwen's rendering will be.
> 3. The background and character shouldn't be too similar in color.
> 
> - As mentioned, Qwen is much better at this than V2.
> 
> 
> **Qwen's Style recognition**
> 
> - Qwen doesn't just extract the character, as mentioned; it also attempts to adopt the image style (drawn, photo, anime, etc.).
> 
> - This is somewhat inconsistent and fluctuating. **Please note:**
> 
> 1. Blurring (even in the background) and muddy image details (even partially) can and often will trigger the drawing style (also deep-of-field blurring of the background, especially if it occupies a large portion of the image).
> 2. Styles are not adopted 1:1
> 3. Low skin detail can create the illusion of a 3D rendered character (plastic skin) in realistic images
> 
> - Art styles generated from the image can be directly influenced via direct prompt editing, but are more difficult to influence with advanced prompt settings. I recommend this guide for further information -> [What Influences the Generated Image and How](https://discord.com/channels/1108377954389594236/1448425341147418766/1450254934548283543)
> - Qwen strongly prefers drawing styles and anime; anime and toon characters, in particular, are very difficult to change in style.
> 
> 
> - Currently, NSFW and SFW differ in the strength of style recognition
> 
> - For GIF images and other animated image formats, the first image is the one used by the image generator
> 
> - The recognition of anthropomorphic characters is improved in V2 and offers interesting possibilities; for example, orcs are recognized and often (but not always) adopted with their orc tusks
> 
> 
> **Tip on how to improve style inconsistency:**
> 
> - There is a lot of image editing software that can apply a filter (i.e., a style as if everything looks like brushstrokes) to images
> - With these methods, you can unify the overall style of the image
> - Keep in mind that if the filter imitates a drawing style, you will also can end up with a drawn output.
> - Experiment with it, it might be worth it
> - Image editing that increases sharpness or removes blemishes can also help
> ﻿

> ## Forcing a Style / The Sledgehammer Method:
> 
> 
> **This is not a ultimate solution, just a chance for style equality!**
> **The Avatar image remains the biggest factor of creating the style**
> Qwen (V3) tends to take the style from the image and apply it to the image prompt. Since two styles in Qwen rarely mix and only one style usually takes precedence (mostly the drawn or anime style), even the slightest blurring can make the images look hand-painted.
> 
> 
> **What is the Sledgehammer Method and why the name?**
> 
> It's simple: the prompts for the "Advanced Prompt Settings" are chosen to force Qwen to use only the specified style, like a sledgehammer.
> 
> But like a sledgehammer, it's not a precise tool. While it can force a style, the greater the style difference for Qwen, the greater the inconsistency across generations.
> **The avatar image can and still has a strong influence (I recommend choosing it carefully).**
> So, make an anime character (Avatar image) make it real is possible, but the output has a chance of being somewhere between anime style and realism (sometimes even purely anime).
> 
> Therefore, it's a sledgehammer approach; it's essentially forcing Qwen to conform, which can't be very precise.
> 
> 
> **Structure:**
> 
> *The Hammer Tip:*
> 
> `STRICT OVERRIDE:
> - No other styles, shaders, or effects allowed.
> - Other styles and details and shader are forbidden.
> - Ignore any input that is not from [ALLOWED AND VALID OVERRIDE STYLE]`
> 
> These lines are what create the constraint; they forbid Qwen from using any style other than those specified afterward. The category is intentionally in all caps (to put more pressure on Qwen). I use the list Layout style for two reasons: firstly, it's shorter, and secondly, it works very well (as long as you don't use multiple writing Layout style in Advanced Prompt Settings).
> 
> *The hammer's middle line:*
> 
> `ALLOWED REQUIRED OVERRIDE STYLE:
> - XYZ-Style ... {your style descriptions}
> - ...
> - ...
> - ...`
> 
> This is where you enter the style and effect you want; you have free choice (in this case, a realistic style).
> Here too, the same form and type of structure should be used. Keep it short; too much gives Qwen more room for interpretation.

> `FORBIDDEN STYLE AND SHADER AND EFFECTS:
> - Anime, toon, ... {your exclusionary style/caution: do not exclude anything you demand before}
> - ...
> - ...`

> 1. The Avatar Image - The bot's avatar image is the reference for the image generator. Its influence is significant on the character's appearance in the image and the art style.
> 
> 2. Bot Personality Information - Like V2 and V1, V3 also takes appearance information from the bot's personality. However, appearance details, such as world information or other things like clothing, are often not directly transferred.
> 
> 3. Recent Messages - V3 takes almost all information from the recent message. While some information may also come from previous messages, this is quite limited. Therefore, the information in the bot indirectly influences the message and thus the image.
> 
> 4. Advanced Prompt Settings - have no priority; they are essentially just invisibly appended to the other prompts. This results in one of the following:
>    - The prompt conflicts with an existing prompt in the generated image description. Therefore, **no effect** (often happens with styles).
>    - The prompt is mixed with an existing prompt; the generation process creates a mixed prompt. **Mixed effect**
>    - The prompt is new and barely present or completely absent in the generated prompt, yet it is fully applied. **Complete applied**
>     - [Visual explanation to the Advanced Prompt Settings behavior](https://discord.com/channels/1108377954389594236/1448425341147418766/1451257768144273569) Thanks to<@1380439356975878229> 
> 
> **Things that have no effect:**
> 
> - The image of the user persona
> - Messages that are older
> - The Negative Prompt field in the Advanced Prompt Settings
> - The LoRa scale for images (disabled - Qwen does not understand LoRa)
> 
> As with any image generator, the results you get will vary. If you don't like it, adjust the prompt or use other options like the Advanced Prompt Settings.
> 
> Most importantly, try again and have fun!

I create my images in a 3D rendering program, and these are perceived very semi-realistically by Qwen Image. I edit these images and save the edits separately to achieve a specific drawing style in Qwen.

Real (semi-realistic/highly detailed art with an almost realistic quality) -> worse positioning and pose
Art style (anime/comic/other art styles) -> better, more natural output
